entries.title: Show HN: Witr – Explain why a process is running on your Linux system
entries.author: pranshuparmar
entries.current_title: Show HN: Witr – Explain why a process is running on your Linux system
entries.excerpt: Hi HN, I built a small Linux CLI tool called witr (Why Is This Running?). The idea came from a situation most of us have hit: you log into a machine, see a process or port running, and immediately wonder why it exists, who started it, and what is keeping it alive right now. witr traces a process, service, or port back to its origin and responsibility chain and explains it in a way that’s quick to read, especially when you’re debugging under pressure. entries.guide_zh: Witr 解释 Linux 进程为何运行、由谁启动，追踪看不懂的后台活动。

entries.title: Show HN: Z80-μLM, a 'Conversational AI' That Fits in 40KB
entries.author: quesomaster9000
entries.current_title: Show HN: Z80-μLM, a 'Conversational AI' That Fits in 40KB
entries.excerpt: How small can a language model be while still doing something useful? I wanted to find out, and had some spare time over the holidays. Z80-μLM is a character-level language model with 2-bit quantized weights ({-2,-1,0,+1}) that runs on a Z80 with 64KB RAM. The entire thing: inference, weights, chat UI, it all fits in a 40KB .COM file that you can run in a CP/M emulator and hopefully even real hardware! It won't write your emails, but it can be trained to play a stripped down
entries.guide_zh: Z80-μLM 将字符语言模型压缩到 40KB，在 Z80 上尝试微型“对话 AI”。

entries.title: Show HN: Minimalist editor that lives in browser, stores everything in the URL
entries.author: medv
entries.current_title: Show HN: Minimalist editor that lives in browser, stores everything in the URL
entries.excerpt: I wanted to see how far I could go building a notes app using only what modern browsers already provide – no frameworks, no storage APIs, no build step. What it does: Single HTML file, no deps, 111 loc Notes live in the URL hash (shareable links!) Auto-compressed with CompressionStream Plain-text editor (contenteditable) History support Page title from first # heading Respects light/dark mode No storage, cookies, or tracking The entire app is the page source. https://textarea
entries.guide_zh: 极简浏览器编辑器把笔记存在 URL 片段中，单个 HTML 文件即可分享与使用。

entries.title: Show HN: Picknplace.js, an alternative to drag-and-drop
entries.author: bbx
entries.current_title: Show HN: Picknplace.js, an alternative to drag-and-drop
entries.excerpt: I find that the drag and drop experience can quickly become a nightmare, especially on mobile. To tap, hold, drag, and scroll, all at the same time, is both difficult to achieve, and prone to errors. I've always had in mind this 2-step approach, where picking an element and placing it were two separate steps. So I implemented this basic version to showcase my idea. While it might take more time than a regular drag and drop, the benefit is for people who struggle with holding
entries.guide_zh: Picknplace.js 把拖放拆成先选后放两步，减少手机上边拖边滚的操作困难。

entries.title: Show HN: WalletWallet – create Apple passes from anything
entries.author: alentodorov
entries.current_title: Show HN: WalletWallet – create Apple passes from anything
entries.excerpt: I got my Apple developer certificate and built a simple app to solve a problem I had. One shop I buy from doesn't have Apple Wallet passes. Since you need signed certificates to build these very simple things, I created a minimal app that signs them. It's available if you need it too. It won't scan cards with AI - you manually enter the barcode, which I think makes it less prone to error.
entries.guide_zh: WalletWallet 为没有 Apple Wallet 支持的卡券生成已签名通行证。
